correctness.rationale: The complete H-representation is verified in Gill--Linusson Thm. 3 and Torres Thm. 3.1. Independent Frobenius projection and determinant calculations yield both squared semiaxis branches and the exact k²≤(n+1)(n−k)² boundary. The orbit contact weights have zero first moment and identity covariance after normalizing the ellipsoid, hence by John’s theorem prove global optimality and uniqueness against nonsymmetric/off-center ellipsoids, not merely within an assumed symmetry class. n=2,k=1, equality cases n=h²−1,k=h(h−1), and k=n exclusion checked; finite cases are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original as an exact intrinsic John ellipsoid classification of every square fixed-cardinality k-assignment polytope for 1<=k<n: two modes, sharp round-to-anisotropic phase, all tangencies, John weights and volume. Same-object prior work gives H-representation and Euclidean inradii but not the determinant-optimal nonround mode. Relevant general orbit/polar and full-dimensional matching-polytope John theorems do not imply this fixed-sum slice result without a fresh calculation. Priority is qualified for unindexed matrix-section/optimal-design literature.
residual_risks: Earlier exact John formulas could exist under optimal-design, transportation-section, k-rook or truncated Birkhoff terminology not found in bounded searches.
The submitted proof applies classical contact decomposition and elementary concave optimization to known facets; originality is the all-parameter explicit solution, not the general method.
The already published inradius work has exactly the same transition threshold, so that threshold alone is not original.
The related full-dimensional and graph-spectral ellipsoid results could motivate a derivation, although their stated theorems do not directly imply this affine-slice classification.

value.rationale: Fixed-k assignment polytopes are natural combinatorial-optimization polytopes with a motivated Frobenius metric; their entire all-integer-family John ellipsoid is a substantive exact geometric invariant. It gives both irreducible eigenspace semiaxes, explicit determinant/volume, a sharp round-to-anisotropic threshold and precise tangent-facet orbits. Inradius alone supplies only the smaller semiaxis and cannot determine this anisotropic maximum-volume configuration. This natural full-family exact classification is useful independent of a broader theorem.

limitations: Only n×n, integer n≥2 and 1≤k<n; intrinsic Frobenius affine-hull metric of dimension n²−1.
Perfect matching k=n has a different lower-dimensional affine hull and is excluded.
